sections.heading: C — Turning, signals, space cushion
sections.markdown:
## C — Turning, signals, space cushion

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Two opposing vehicles signaling left turns pass in front of each other with their passenger sides beside each other [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Before any U-turn, check for No U-Turn or No Left Turn signs; in business districts, cities, and towns U-turns are allowed only at intersections, and never on a highway [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
To U-turn, signal left, stop, yield to approaching traffic, and when clear enter the outside or right-hand lane of the opposite direction [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
Turn signals are required by law for lane changes, turns, and highway entries and exits; use them or hand signals even with no traffic around, and cancel the signal after finishing [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
Signal three or four seconds, 100 feet, before your turn, and stay alert for drivers who may pull out misjudging where you will turn [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
Hand signals use the left arm: straight out for a left turn, pointing up for a right turn, and pointing down for slowing or stopping [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
Over-correcting steers more sharply than expected and slides the rear wheels outward, risking control loss; slow down on curves, and if you veer off, ease off speed without panic, look where you want to go, and steer back slowly [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A01
Turn right from the lane furthest right: signal three or four seconds, 100 feet, ahead, look left and right for pedestrians and traffic, brake before and during, stop fully at red lights and stop signs, and enter the lane closest to the curb unless markings lead otherwise [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A01
Turn left from the furthest left lane into the leftmost lane unless markings or multiple turn lanes direct otherwise: signal three or four seconds, 100 feet, ahead, look all ways including opposite traffic, hold wheels straight until committed, and yield to opposite vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A02
Build a space cushion by centering your lane and keeping room ahead and behind so vehicles can pass or stop safely [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A02
On dry roads follow at 2 seconds under 35 MPH, 3 seconds from 35 to 45, and 4 seconds from 46 to 70; the rule fails above 70 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A02
Time your gap from a fixed object the car ahead passes: arriving early means too close, so slow and widen; add seconds for bad weather, heavy traffic, poor pavement, or a poor vehicle [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A02
Hand response runs near a half second and foot response near three-quarters, before perception delays from tiredness, medication, or distraction; conditions, speed, alertness, and vehicle weight all change stopping [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A02
Widen following distance behind vision-blocking large vehicles, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting expressways, behind motorcycles or bicycles, and when being tailgated [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A02
When tailgated, never brake suddenly: move over or tap the brakes to flash and slow; help followers with a steady speed and brake taps before slowing or stopping [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A02
Search the whole scene with moving eyes, focus 20 to 30 seconds ahead or about one city block, and scan side to side for signs, signals, cars, and people [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A02
Read road clues like exhaust smoke, brake or backup lights, and turned wheels; watch for pedestrians, bicyclists, and slow vehicles, and in rural areas for hidden junctions, curves, hills, trucks, and farm equipment [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A02
Enter intersections with a left-right-left look, left first as the nearer threat; check the rearview about every 10 seconds and before lane changes, backing, quick slows, and long descents [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]
